guide.summary: Internal tool in your own workspace (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public app, installed by any workspace, unlisted (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Commercial agent listed in Slack Marketplace (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal tool in your own workspace (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Commercial agent listed in Slack Marketplace (app review).

composio.note: Composio has a managed Slack app, fine for prototypes. Users then see Composio's name on the consent screen and share quota with other Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio provides a managed Slack app. For launch you need your own app, because the Marketplace listing, your branding and your own rate-limit quota all belong to your app.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio
Dedicated quota instead of shared quota
Marketplace listing and review belong to your own app

prerequisites.title: 10 active workspaces before Marketplace submission
prerequisites.detail: You must first run the app on 10 or more active workspaces, so plan to distribute unlisted first. Otherwise submission is blocked.

prerequisites.title: Finished, tested app with public pages
prerequisites.detail: Do not submit unfinished apps. You also need a public landing page.

prerequisites.title: Test accounts, demo and scope reasons
prerequisites.detail: Prepare test accounts with dummy data, a demo video of install and OAuth, and a reason for every scope.

prerequisites.title: AI disclosures for the listing
prerequisites.detail: If the agent uses generative AI, you must disclose model and data handling in the submission.

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed Slack
steps.detail: Use the Composio managed app to validate the agent before registering anything.
steps.done_when: Agent can call Slack tools in a test account.

steps.title: Create Slack app and list minimal scopes
steps.detail: Create the app in Slack's app settings and pick the fewest scopes the agent needs. Draft a reason for each scope.
steps.done_when: App exists with client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Add the redirect URL copied from the Composio dashboard to the Slack app.
steps.done_when: A test user completes OAuth with your app.

steps.title: Distribute and gather 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Enable distribution and get customers installing and using the app. Check how many unlisted installs you have.
steps.done_when: 10 workspaces used in the last 28 days.

steps.title: Prepare submission materials
steps.detail: Draft scope justifications, listing copy, demo script and privacy policy outline. Include an architecture diagram to speed up review.

steps.title: Record demo and submit
steps.detail: Record the demo, set up test accounts and submit from the app's Marketplace section.

steps.title: Wait for Slack review
steps.detail: Preliminary review, then functional review. Answer any feedback.

traps.title: For commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace
traps.detail: For commercially distributed apps not approved for the Marketplace and created after May 29, 2025 (or newly installed), conversations.history and conversations.replies are limited to 1 request per minute.

traps.title: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes
traps.detail: The temporary authorization code expires after ten minutes.

traps.title: Review is slow and cannot be accelerated
traps.detail: Official limits are 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks, and developers report 4-5 months. Slack will not speed it up for your launch date.

traps.title: Fixes reset your place in the preliminary queue
traps.detail: Every resubmission during the preliminary stage restarts the wait, so polish the listing first.

traps.title: Broad scopes are likely to be refused
traps.detail: History, file and search scopes get enhanced review, and restricted scopes are not accepted. Admin scopes are unlikely to be approved.

traps.title: New unlisted installs hit 1 request per minute
traps.detail: Commercially distributed unlisted apps get a 15-object, 1-request-per-minute limit on conversation history methods for new installs. That breaks most reading agents.

traps.title: Storing or training on Slack data
traps.detail: Agent apps must not store Slack data, and apps training LLMs on it are unsuitable.

traps.title: Changes after launch need re-review
traps.detail: The live version is locked, and scope or feature changes require resubmission.

blockers.what_it_means: The app does not yet have 10 active workspaces.
blockers.what_to_do: Distribute unlisted and get customers using the app until 10 workspaces have been active.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft an onboarding plan for pilot customers.

blockers.what_it_means: The app is not distributed, so it installs only on its owner workspace.
blockers.what_to_do: Enable public distribution in the app settings.

blockers.symptom: Org-level install blocked for a member
blockers.what_it_means: Org-level installs may require an Org Owner or Org Admin.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's org admin to install.
blockers.agent_can_help: Write instructions for the customer admin.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: we created an advanced Security Review program that may be performed on published Slack Marketplace applications.
evidence.answer: The Security Review program may be performed on published Slack Marketplace applications; the page gives no user, install or scope threshold that triggers it.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: As part of our security review process, we will assess the security of all parts of your infrastructure that are required to make the core functionality of your offering work in its intended manner (both the Slack parts, and yours).
evidence.answer: The review assesses the security of all parts of the infrastructure required for the core functionality to work as intended, both Slack parts and the developer's parts.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Automated web application security scanning
evidence.answer: Slack reserves the right to run automated web application security scanning on applicable parts of the app.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Automated network security scanning
evidence.answer: Slack reserves the right to run automated network security scanning on applicable parts of the app.

evidence.question: G3

evidence.answer: Slack reserves the right to manually verify that authentication scope requests follow least-privilege design.

evidence.question: G3

evidence.answer: Slack reserves the right to manually test functionality for security vulnerabilities and misuse.

evidence.answer: Slack reserves the right to perform a manual architecture review of the app.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: While not necessary, a basic architecture diagram for your application helps expedite our review process.
evidence.answer: Submitting a basic architecture diagram is optional but speeds up the review; it should cover services that interact with Slack, including servers, databases, and required third-party integrations.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your application must "feature-complete" and function as your final product will function on the Slack Marketplace.
evidence.answer: The app must be feature-complete and must function as the final product will function on the Slack Marketplace.

evidence.question: G3

evidence.question: G3

evidence.answer: Apps must not give people access to information or abilities they would not otherwise have in Slack.
